title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 60 (Publication of Authorised, Subscribed and Paid-Up Capital)

content.overview: Section 60 requires that where any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company, such notice or document must also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up.
content.glance: If authorised capital is stated in notices, ads or stationery, subscribed and paid-up capital must also be stated equally prominently.
content.study: Where any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper, of a company contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company, such notice or document shall also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up. Default attracts penalty. Current-law framing: check whether authorised capital is stated; if so, require equally prominent subscribed and paid-up figures.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Any notice, advertisement, official publication, business letter, billhead or letter paper that states authorised capital.

sections.heading: Requirement
sections.body: Must also state subscribed capital and paid-up capital in an equally prominent position and equally conspicuous characters.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Prevents misleading impression of the company’s capital strength by stating only authorised capital.

provisions.title: Publication of authorised, subscribed and paid-up capital

examples.title: Compliant stationery
examples.body: Letter paper states authorised ₹10 crore, subscribed ₹6 crore and paid-up ₹5 crore in equally prominent characters. Section 60 is complied with.

examples.title: Misleading advertisement
examples.body: An advertisement states only ‘Authorised capital ₹100 crore’ without subscribed or paid-up figures. Section 60 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company advertise only its authorised capital?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. If authorised capital is stated, subscribed and paid-up must also be stated equally prominently under s. 60.

distinctions.title: Publication of capital (s. 60) vs alteration of capital (s. 61)
distinctions.left: How capital figures must be disclosed in publications
distinctions.right: How share capital may be altered (increase, consolidate, sub-divide, cancel)

misconceptions.trap: Stating authorised capital alone is always fine.
misconceptions.correction: Section 60 requires subscribed and paid-up to be stated equally prominently whenever authorised capital is stated.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 60 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify publication stating authorised capital. II. Check presence and prominence of subscribed and paid-up. III. Conclude compliance or breach.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Document; capital statements; prominence comparison; precise relief.
